topics.flagship-ru-ua: The UK government warned that businesses supplying Ukraine's armed forces could become targets of Russian sabotage and urged them to 'act now' (4 outlets). Zelenskiy confirmed a Ukrainian drone strike on a cargo ship in the Gulf of Finland owned by a firm that provides logistics for Russia's defence ministry, and Ukraine is reportedly targeting Russian military networks in Africa, including Libya, Sudan and Mali. Russia accused NATO member Estonia of hostile actions 'on the verge of unleashing open war' over border measures, with Tallinn due to close road crossings from Dec. 1, while NATO allies are reportedly voicing anxiety about the war spreading.
topics.flagship-ir-il: A Saudi skyscraper was hit again in an attack Saudi civil defence blamed on the Houthis, injuring 11, and the coalition called it a 'terrorist attack' (11 outlets). Israeli airstrikes in Gaza killed seven, including a senior Hamas security official and two police officers, and a separate Khan Yunis strike reportedly killed three. Israeli Defense Minister Katz said Iran is developing chemical weapons and plotting to kill Trump but cannot yet strike Israel with them, while Eisenkot saw no immediate threat requiring action. A single-outlet opinion interview disputes the Iranian chemical-weapons reports.
topics.T15: The lead item, from a single outlet, covers online doomsday rumors of a 90-day blackout; FEMA and other federal officials say there is no evidence of a secret emergency and that the recent outages were unrelated technical issues. A magnitude 7.1 earthquake reportedly struck southern Japan with no tsunami detected (the caption is dated July 28, 2026, so timing is unclear). Other items are minor: a second Colorado major disaster declaration request after flooding, a magnitude 5.1 quake in the Philippines, a New Zealand flood concern, and Red Cross anticipatory-action work in the Americas.
topics.T01: Coverage is sparse and mixed, with no single dominant conflict story. A report says new landmine use and production are undermining the ban treaty, and Amnesty alleges Ethiopian shelling of Alamata in Tigray may amount to war crimes. Russian warplanes reportedly triggered an air-raid alert on South Korea's Ulleung Island, and Kim Jong Un has reportedly ignored Trump's overtures for over a year.
topics.T02: Land mine casualties are rising in Syria two years after the war, with nearly 1,000 children among those killed or injured (2 outlets). The WFP warned that wars are choking food routes, threatening aid for 7.3 million people, and a UN report found about 47,000 women and girls were killed by relatives in 2025. Other items include an attack on a cattle camp in South Sudan, Rohingya justice after the ICJ ruling, and a toxic liquor death toll of 17 in Manipur.
topics.T03: The stories are mostly institutional or tangential. The UK made a statement at the 31st OPCW Conference of the States Parties, and UN Secretary-General Guterres urged states to stand firm amid growing reports of chemical weapons use. Katz's claim that Iran is developing chemical weapons is covered under the Iran/Israel topic. Other items cover the environmental release from a planned Army lead azide detonation in Iowa and an academic warning about AI and neuroscience being misused for chemical weapons.
topics.T04: A meningitis outbreak has reportedly killed 15 people in Gaza, prompting a public health alert amid infrastructure collapse (2 outlets). Elsewhere, Legionnaires' disease killed two in Rotherham, UK, and animal disease outbreaks were reported in Alberta hares, Russian cattle (lumpy skin disease) and Kentucky deer. Entebbe Airport ran an outbreak-response exercise, and a Nigerian community reported an unidentified skin disease. The Niagara Falls item appears to be an old, COVID-era piece.
topics.T05: Ousted Bangladeshi leader Sheikh Hasina says she plans to return from exile on December 16, while the government says she can only be extradited; Dhaka also told diplomats that 'Awami terrorists' are creating fear (2 outlets and 1). One outlet describes France as facing debt, political and social crises five months before presidential elections. A man at the centre of the Citywest riot case was deported from Ireland to Chad.
topics.T06: Mother and son 'instigators' were jailed for roles in the Ballymena race riots (3 outlets), and India's Supreme Court is to hear bail pleas from Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam in the Delhi riots case (3 outlets). Students rallied in Bangkok on Nov. 20 against Prime Minister Anutin, though one analysis says Thailand lacks the youth joblessness behind unrest elsewhere in Asia. Other items are court rulings on past Indian riots, a UK opposition warning of French-style riots, and Indian opposition threats of protests against Meta.
topics.T07: Coverage is thin and poorly sourced. A single opinion-style piece claims the leaders of China, Russia and the US met in Shenzhen on November 19 and issued a declaration that nuclear war cannot be won. Separately, Russia dismissed as 'unfounded' German media reports that it was about to launch a nuclear weapon into space, with the report carrying no independent sourcing. Neither item is verified.
topics.T08: Russia's FSB said it thwarted a bombing plot against a synagogue in Kislovodsk (2 outlets). Jordan's church leaders cancelled public Christmas celebrations following a terrorist attack, and a State Security Court verdict in the Amman attack case is due Wednesday, with three Islamists reportedly already sentenced to death. A government investigation reportedly found four AI chatbots produced detailed terrorist attack plans.
topics.T10: The Pentagon sharply rebuked Canada over defense spending and its review of the F-35 (2 outlets), and Hegseth's classified memo reportedly requires approval for some social events with Canadians. Australia and the Solomon Islands signed a security pact naming Canberra the 'primary security partner' and ruling out foreign bases, amid reports the Solomons may not renew its China deal in 2027. Other items include Japanese auto suppliers moving into defense and anti-militarization protests in Brussels.
topics.T11: Several multinational exercises are under way or announced. India and Malaysia are conducting Harimau Shakti 2026 with a drone-warfare focus, and India and Sri Lanka are running Mitra Shakti 2026. China and Cambodia will hold Golden Dragon-2026 from late November to mid-December, and Spain's Atlas 26 drill included an Ericsson 5G drone-defence demonstration. A 700-troop exercise also began across Belgium.
topics.T12: The European Commission confirmed attackers breached its EU Academy hub and stole user personal data (2 outlets). Reportedly, hackers may have breached the FBI's NCIC criminal database, and GreyNoise identified a campaign compromising Check Point management servers at at least 22 organizations. The US Coast Guard reportedly boarded two foreign ships whose networks were compromised amid an Iranian hacking probe, and other items cover AI-enabled attacks on Bell and on ports and a Microsoft 365 outage.
topics.T13: Coverage is sparse and largely partisan or opinion-driven, so no clear development emerges. Items include an AfD leader's call for 2.6 million deportations from Germany, a tabloid piece on asylum-seeker housing in English villages, and a zero-source claim of coordinated planning behind the Ceuta migrant swim-ins.
topics.T14: The US warned Americans in the Middle East of Iranian and Houthi attack threats, cautioning of possible flight cancellations, airspace closures and travel disruptions. This is a single-outlet report.
topics.T16: Spain holds a general election Sunday, with polls pointing to a conservative and far-right win over Pedro Sánchez. Reporting on the US midterms describes a Republican defeat, with Thune and Zinke discussing the party's rebuilding and messaging, and in Israel, commentary describes Eisenkot facing Knesset maneuvering and Netanyahu allegedly seeking another vote. Nigeria's 2027 poll prompted warnings about political violence and calls for police neutrality.

bluf: A Saudi skyscraper was hit again in an attack that Saudi civil defence blamed on the Houthis, injuring 11, and the coalition condemned it as a 'terrorist attack' (11 outlets). Land mine casualties are soaring in Syria two years after the war, with nearly 1,000 children among those killed or injured by leftover explosives. Israeli airstrikes in Gaza killed seven, including a senior Hamas security official and two police officers, according to medics and police. Israel's defense minister Katz said Iran is developing chemical weapons and plotting to kill Trump but cannot yet strike Israel with them, while Eisenkot said he saw no immediate threat requiring action. The UK government warned businesses supplying Ukraine's armed forces that they could become targets of Russian sabotage and urged them to 'act now.' Russia accused Estonia of hostile actions 'on the verge of unleashing open war' as Tallinn prepares to close road crossings from Dec. 1, and Zelenskiy confirmed a Ukrainian drone strike on a Russian-linked cargo ship in the Gulf of Finland. The US also warned Americans in the Middle East of Iranian and Houthi attack threats, with possible airspace closures and travel disruptions (reportedly, from a single outlet).
